title: Oncall readiness, SLO drills, and customer notification playbook
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Summary

This playbook describes Redwood Inference's oncall readiness program focused on: SLO-based drills, consistent runbook usage, and standardized customer communications. The goal is to reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to recovery (MTTR) for high-severity incidents while preserving clear, timely customer-facing updates.

Scope

- Applies to production customer-facing services: API gateway, runtime serving layer, model catalog, embedding/embedding service, and the Console.
- Covers incident triage, escalation, internal comms, customer/status page updates, post-incident reviews, and game-day exercises.
- Does not replace service-specific runbooks; instead complements them with a standard escalation and comms pattern.

Quick links (operational)

- PagerDuty: pd://redwood-production
- Status page: https://status.redwoodinference.internal (internal-only)
- Runbook repository: git@repo:redwood/runbooks.git
- Slack channels: #oncall, #incident-ops, #cust-comm

Severity taxonomy and thresholds

We use a four-level severity model tied to customer impact and SLOs. All incidents must be classified within the first 15 minutes.

1) Sev 0 (Critical) — system-wide outage or large customer impact
   - Symptoms: API error rate > 10% global for 5+ minutes OR region-wide unavailability OR sustained >50% SLO breach risk.
   - Pager: immediate page to primary oncall + escalation to engineering leadership. Target MTTR: 60 minutes.

2) Sev 1 (High) — significant degradation affecting many customers
   - Symptoms: latency p95 >2x baseline AND affecting >25% of requests OR model-serving errors cluster.
   - Pager: primary oncall. Target MTTR: 180 minutes.

3) Sev 2 (Medium) — localized degradation or single-customer impact
   - Pager: notify oncall via channel, optional page if not acknowledged. Target MTTR: 24 hours.

4) Sev 3 (Low) — informational, non-urgent issues or scheduled maintenance
   - Handled in backlog; update status page when relevant.

Roles and responsibilities

- Primary Oncall (Engineering): first responder, triage, and runbook execution.
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates responders, decides severity, and approves customer messages for Sev1/Sev0.
- Triage Engineer: collects logs, traces, and initial metrics; creates incident record.
- Comms Lead (Customer Success / IC): drafts status page and customer messages; coordinates with legal if data exposure suspected.
- Escalation Owner (Engineering Lead): implements code/fix or rollback and owns rollout plan.
- Postmortem Owner: ensures follow-up actions and tracks them to completion.

Oncall rotation and handoff (standard practice)

- Rotation length: 1 week for production oncall, 2 weeks for secondary/backfill.
- Handoff checklist (to be completed in Slack at shift start and end):
  1) Confirm Slack/Ding/PD notifications are working.
  2) Verify runbook repo is reachable and pull latest changes: git fetch origin/main && git pull.
  3) Snapshot open incidents and outstanding action items in #oncall-handoff thread.
  4) Confirm contact details for your rotation teammate (mobile and email).

- Warm handoff process: on last day of shift, the outgoing oncall posts a final summary of active alerts, mitigations in progress, and observed anomalies. The incoming oncall must acknowledge and ask clarifying questions within 15 minutes.

Paging and escalation timings

- Initial page: 0 minutes. If not acknowledged in 5 minutes -> escalate to secondary.
- If still not acknowledged in 15 minutes -> page engineering lead.
- For Sev0 incidents, immediately page on-call + engineering leadership and call the IC.

Runbook usage and template (how to run a runbook)

General guidance: Always work from the canonical runbook in the runbook repo. If a runbook is out of date, annotate and file a maintenance ticket.

Runbook template (use as header in each service runbook):

- Purpose: One-sentence description of the incident type covered.
- Detection: Metric/alert that should trigger this runbook (include alert name and thresholds).
- Impact assessment: list of systems/customers affected and quick commands to verify.
- Quick mitigation steps: minimal actions to restore service (prefer config toggles/traffic-shifts over code changes).
- Full remediation steps: longer-term fixes or rollbacks with safety checks.
- Post-incident checks: verification commands and dashboards to observe.
- Owner and runbook last-updated date.

Example: Latency spike runbook (abridged)

1) Detection:
   - Alert: api-latency-p95 > 1200ms for 3m
   - Verify: curl -sS https://api.redwoodinference.internal/health | jq .latency_p95

2) Quick mitigation:
   - Check autoscaling: kubectl get hpa -n serving; if replica count stable, scale deployment: kubectl scale deploy/serving-blue --replicas=8 -n serving
   - If related to batching: toggle batching profile to conservative: /ops/batching toggle --profile conservative --service serving

3) Full remediation:
   - Roll back the latest model-variant rollout: ./deploy/rollout rollback --service serving --to=stable
   - Recompile optimized kernels if CPU/GPU saturation observed: follow kernel compile playbook in /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling

4) Post-incident checks:
   - Verify p95 latency back to baseline for 15m.
   - Monitor errors and token-per-second metrics for 60m.

Customer-facing communication templates

Use these templates as the basis for status page and direct customer comms. The Comms Lead must edit and approve before publishing. Keep messages clear, factual, and free of speculation.

Status page incident (short)

- Title: [Investigating] Intermittent API errors affecting generation endpoints
- Impact: A subset of API requests may return 500 errors or time out. Affects ~30% of requests across regions.
- Next update: in 30 minutes
- Update example: 2025-03-15T14:20Z — We have identified a service degradation impacting generation endpoints and initiated a rollback of the recent model rollout. Our engineering team is monitoring recovery.

Direct customer message (email/CS rep template)

Subject: Incident affecting Redwood API responses — update

Hello <CustomerName>,

We are investigating an incident that may cause intermittent 500 errors and timeouts when calling the Redwood API. Our oncall team has put mitigations in place and we are monitoring recovery. We will provide another update within 30 minutes.

Impact: you may see failed requests or delays for requests routed to the affected variant.

If you have a production-critical integration and need assistance: reply to this email or contact your Customer Success representative.

We apologize for the disruption and will follow up with a post-incident summary.

Commands and artifacts for comms lead

- Compose status page JSON (example snippet):
{
  "status": "investigating",
  "components": ["API"],
  "incident_updates": [{"body": "Investigating increased 500 errors on generation endpoints.", "created_at": "2025-03-15T14:20:00Z"}]
}

- Slack update: /topic status: Investigating API errors — rollback in progress.

Postmortem and action tracking (RCA checklist)

Postmortem must be filed within 72 hours for Sev1/Sev0 incidents and include:

- Summary: concise incident overview (what, when, impact).
- Timeline: ordered events with timestamps and actors.
- Root cause analysis: 5 whys + contributing factors.
- Mitigations implemented during incident.
- Long-term actions (owner and due date).
- Postmortem severity and lessons learned.

RCA checklist: verify instrumentation coverage, reproduce in staging where safe, confirm alert thresholds, and schedule follow-up engineering review.

Game day program (SLO drills)

Purpose: validate we can detect, escalate, and communicate incidents quickly and that runbooks are accurate.

Cadence and roles:
- Quarterly company-wide game day (table-top style) led by Eng SRE.
- Monthly team-level drills (2 hours) covering a single service and the comms template.
- Participants: oncall engineers, secondary, engineering lead, product owner, and customer success.

Example drill (90 minutes)
- 00:00 — Inject synthetic latency (or simulated alert) into serving metrics.
- 00:05 — Oncall is paged; triage starts.
- 00:15 — IC declared; comms lead drafts status page entry.
- 00:30 — Mitigation (traffic shift to warm pool) executed.
- 00:50 — Recovery verified; postmortem owner assigned.
- 01:30 — Retrospective and runbook edits.

Game day evaluation criteria:
- Acknowledge time < 3 minutes
- Severity classification accuracy > 90%
- Comms sent within 30 minutes of IC declaration
- Runbook fidelity score (did steps match observed behavior?) — pass/fail

Monitoring, dashboards, and SLOs

Key SLOs (examples):
- API availability SLO: 99.95% monthly for production generation endpoints
- Latency SLO: p95 < 600ms for text-generation calls (90% of traffic)
- Embedding correctness: regression test suite pass rate >= 99% on model updates

Suggested dashboards:
- Global overview: total requests, error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec
- Model health: recent rollouts, variant split, and rollback status
- Resource saturation: GPU utilization, OOM events, queue length

Alert hygiene and tuning

- Every alert must map to an SLO or a clear operational signal (no alert should exist without an owner).
- Alert thresholds must include suppression windows and runbook links.
- Quarterly review of noisy alerts: if an alert fires more than 10 times per month, file a tuning ticket.

Post-incident follow-up and tracking

- Use the incident tracker board (Jira project: OPS-INCIDENTS) to create a parent ticket for each Sev1/Sev0 with linked remediation tasks.
- Track actions to completion and review in the monthly reliability meeting.
- For every change to a runbook, add a one-line changelog entry at the top and increment the version.

Appendices

A) Sample kubectl and tracing commands
- kubectl -n serving get pods -o wide
- kubectl -n serving logs deployment/serving-blue --tail 200 | grep ERROR
- ./tools/trace-query --trace-id <trace-id> --service serving

B) Status page examples and language matrix (short/medium/long)
- Short: Investigating — intermittent API errors affecting generation endpoints.
- Medium: Our oncall team has identified an increase in 500 responses for generation endpoints, likely related to a model rollout. We are rolling back and monitoring recovery. Next update in 30 minutes.
- Long: We have identified a service degradation following a model variant rollout that affects a subset of requests. Mitigation (rollback) is in progress. There is no evidence of data loss. We will provide a timeline and RCA after stabilization.

C) Quick checklist for IC when data exposure suspected
- Contact Security and Legal immediately.
- Freeze logs/archives for the affected window.
- Use template: "Potential data exposure — contact security immediately" in Slack and PD.

D) Runbook maintenance SLA
- Owners must review and sign off runbooks quarterly. Missing owner triggers escalation to service lead.

Contact list (oncall escalation)

- Oncall team alias: oncall@redwoodinference.internal
- Escalation lead: eng-lead@redwoodinference.internal
- Customer comms: cust-success@redwoodinference.internal
